messages:
Jordan (cust-jordan): Hey team, we're seeing a spike of 502/504s from the hosted inference endpoint for our app since ~2024-10-12T09:05Z. Customer reports: requests hang for ~10-15s then 502 gateway. curl shows TLS handshake timeout. Example curl output: `curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` -> `* TCP_NODELAY set` then `* Connection timed out after 10001 ms` and TLS not completed. Any known rollouts?

Alex (support): Thanks Jordan — can you paste the exact request ID / sample request header? Also did you notice any client IP/common region?

Jordan (cust-jordan): Request ID: req-0a1b2c3d. Most failures from us-east-1. We've validated retry logic and backoff; this is reproducible from our side. Tried from two networks and same outcome.

deploy-bot: Deployment: cert-rotation-service v2.3.1 rolled at 2024-10-12T08:58Z (user: infra-deploy). No automatic rollback.

Sam (oncall_sre): Noted. @Maya please triage. Preliminary hypothesis: cert rotation may have left an incomplete chain on some edge nodes or upstream resolver returned stale A records during the rollout window. Jordan, can you run `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example:443 -servername api.redwood.example -brief` and paste output? Also `dig +trace api.redwood.example` would help.

Jordan (cust-jordan): Paste below. openssl output: ```CONNECTED(00000003) depth=2 C = US, O = ExampleCA, CN = Example CA Root verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate --- No client certificate CA names sent --- SSL handshake has read 0 bytes and written 292 bytes --- New, (NONE), Cipher is (NONE) ``` dig: shows an A record that flips between 10.11.12.13 and 127.0.0.53 depending on resolver.

Maya (eng-sre): That openssl output suggests the server didn't send the full chain (client couldn't verify). But "SSL handshake has read 0 bytes" can also indicate the TLS connection didn't progress (RST or timeout). The dig flipping to 127.0.0.53 points to local systemd-resolved stub resolver being returned in some paths or DNS misconfiguration. Two parallel issues possible: (1) edge nodes with incomplete chain after rotation, (2) recursive resolver returning invalid address causing route to blackhole.

Alex (support): Jordan — does `curl --resolve` to pin an IP reproduce? `curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example:443:10.11.12.13 https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate`

Jordan (cust-jordan): Good idea. With `--resolve` to 10.11.12.13 the request completes successfully (latency ~120ms). With the other IP (127.0.0.53) it fails immediately.

Maya (eng-sre): Confirmed: that points to DNS resolver poisoning or TTL mismatch during the edge BGP/proxy rotation. Also need to verify cert chain on 10.11.12.13 vs other nodes. Sam, can you run `curl -Iv` and `openssl s_client` from our monitoring probes in us-east to both addresses?

Sam (oncall_sre): Running probes now. Quick paste: probe -> 10.11.12.13: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` TLS chain includes full intermediates. probe -> 127.0.0.53: connection fails at TCP (RST) or local routing. Also saw `SERVFAIL` from one of our recursive resolvers for api.redwood.example at 09:06Z.

DevEx-Bot: Alert: increased 5xx errors for /v1/generate, rate +18% in last 10m, error class: TLS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT, top client region: us-east-1.

Maya (eng-sre): Action plan: 1) Roll back the cert rotation on the small subset of edge nodes that reported incomplete chain, 2) purge internal DNS caches and bump resolver TTL on the zone to 30s while we complete rotation, 3) add temporary IP-based fallback in our edge routing policy for health checks to avoid sending traffic to resolvers returning loopback. Jordan — can you confirm whether your SDK is respecting the `A` records TTL or using a long-lived cache?

Jordan (cust-jordan): Our SDK caches for 5 minutes by default, but we do backoff + cache invalidation on connection errors. We saw cached 127.0.0.53 entries after the initial fail, which prolonged issues for about ~3 minutes until we manually flushed.

Alex (support): Steps we executed: - Infra rolled back partial certs for subset nodes at 09:28Z - DNS team purged caches and increased SOA serial / lowered TTL at 09:35Z - Edge routing added fallback to healthy pool at 09:42Z.

Maya (eng-sre): Follow-ups: - We'll open INC-24319 to track a permanent fix for cert rotation orchestration to ensure full-chain is pushed atomically. - DNS team to investigate why some resolvers returned 127.0.0.53 (likely a misconfguration/EDNS/forwarder). - Add probe to detect mismatched chains across all edge nodes.

Jordan (cust-jordan): After your rollback + DNS purge our production traffic returned to normal at ~09:48Z. Thanks all — please confirm when INC is created so we can reference it in the postmortem.

Sam (oncall_sre): INC-24319 created and assigned to eng-sre. Tags: tls, dns, cert-rotation, customer-impact.

Maya (eng-sre): For engineers: quick reproducer curl commands used during triage: ```# replicate TLS timeout (bad DNS) curl -v --connect-timeout 10 https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate # pin to good host curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example:443:10.11.12.13 https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate # debug certificate chain openssl s_client -connect 10.11.12.13:443 -servername api.redwood.example -showcerts ``` Also logs to check on edge: `/var/log/nginx/edge-tls.log` and `edge-proxy: handshake_failures` metric.

Alex (support): I'll follow up with the customer and share the incident link and rollback summary. Thanks team :thumbsup:

Jordan (cust-jordan): Appreciated — please include mitigation note about shorter DNS TTL during rotation and advise customers to implement aggressive DNS failure handling (immediate cache flush on handshake errors)."
